current_text.html: When a Presbytery shall divest a minister of his office without censure, or depose him without excommunication, it shall assign him to membership in some particular church, subject to the approval of the Session of that church.
current_text.text: When a Presbytery shall divest a minister of his office without censure, or depose him without excommunication, it shall assign him to membership in some particular church, subject to the approval of the Session of that church.

relationships.title: Membership status and session authority upon dissolution of a congregation

occurrences.excerpt: Upon dissolution of a congregation, the session terminates, membership in the visible church is dissolved for those not transferred, and Presbytery may not unilaterally assign members to other churches.

relationships.title: Hann v. Pee Dee Presbytery

topics: complainant not subject to presbytery jurisdiction
metadata.synopsis: Kristin Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery was dismissed because the SJC held she lacked standing: she was not subject to Pee Dee Presbytery's jurisdiction, so the complaint was judicially out of order and could not be put in order. The SJC made no merits ruling and stated that the ruling did not stay Presbytery's continuing investigation or review of resulting actions. The adopted ruling was approved 17-2; Maynard and Sartorius dissented without stated reasons, four were absent, and Ross recused.

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

metadata.synopsis: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

relationships.title: Presbyterian Church in America v. South Florida Presbytery (Citation)

occurrences.excerpt: Grounds: As written, this action appears to violate BCO 46-8. (Note: A response to this exception should be sent to the 45th General Assembly as part of the normal review process.)

topics: citation for failure to respond to exceptions
metadata.synopsis: Reviewing South Florida Presbytery’s response to a General Assembly citation, the SJC found most responses satisfactory but rejected one because it did not address BCO 32-2’s requirement to proceed once a charge is made. It approved previously unsubmitted 2009 executive-session minutes with an exception because their treatment of a teaching elder appeared to violate BCO 46-8. Presbytery also had to submit amended minutes and complete, or formally plan, overdue Session-record reviews for report to the 45th General Assembly.

relationships.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. He reverted to membership under pending indictment. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning.

relationships.title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: 5. Did GLP err at its May 4, 2013 Stated Meeting by not assigning TE Gonzales “to membership in some particular church...." pursuant to BCO 46-8?

topics: lack of acceptance to the Church
habitual failure to perform official functions
metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture.

metadata.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.

relationships.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

relationships.title: Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed convictions for contumacy and threatening elders with civil litigation, plus deposition and excommunication. The SJC sustained contumacy as failure to remain subject to the brethren under the ordination vow, not BCO 32-6-type contumacy. It sustained deposition but found excommunication excessive given the conflict and replaced it with indefinite suspension from the sacraments. It did not sustain the threat conviction because the attorney’s letter was absent from the record. A dissent disputed the contumacy ruling.

relationships.title: Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

topics: suspension of session without due process
metadata.synopsis: Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen.

relationships.title: Melton et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery

topics: higher court authority over local church
metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged the ruling of the session of Westminster Presbyterian Church (Chattanooga) disallowing proxy votes at a December 10, 1989 congregational meeting that voted not to rescind the earlier dissolution and property transfer to New City Fellowship. The SJC denied all specifications, holding that proxy voting was not required under BCO 24-4 or Robert's Rules, and that the congregation's decision to dissolve was within its rights under BCO Chapter 25.

metadata.synopsis: Randy Stringer appealed his excommunication by Mississippi Valley Presbytery after being deposed and then excommunicated for failure to respond to the presbytery. The SJC set aside the excommunication and remanded the case to MVP, holding that after deposition the presbytery was required under BCO 46-8 to assign Stringer to membership in a particular church rather than proceed to excommunication. Dr. Morton H. Smith dissented, arguing that the presbytery had proper grounds to proceed to excommunication after Stringer's contumacy.
